title: Level
description: Canonical level definition for the Game Boy RPG level editor and compiler.

id.description: Unique identifier for the level/scene (e.g. forest, town, field)

default_walkable.description: Ground tile for every cell the terrain layer leaves unpainted (tileset.tile_id format, e.g. forest.forest_plain_floor_2). Declared once per level; the editor fill, the compiler expansion, the ROM fallback rendering, and the parity gate all use this one field. When absent, tools fall back to the first tile with 'plain' in the manifest order.

music.description: Background music track enum (e.g. MUSIC_OVERWORLD, MUSIC_TOWN, MUSIC_DUNGEON)

map_id.description: Engine MapId enum constant (e.g. MAP_FOREST, MAP_TOWN)

obj_palettes.description: Sparse per-map OBJ (sprite) palette overrides: hardware slot 0-7 -> artist ramp name (e.g. {"6": "sprites10"}). Slots absent here keep the palette_slots.json default. Declaring is how maps that need a different ramp in a shared slot (dog red vs merchant orange in slot 6) pick their winner; the ROM programs these on every scene load.

terrain.description: 2D tile grid array of strings (rows of semantic tile IDs) or list of block placements

blocks.description: Optional explicit list of SceneTerrainBlock rects

entry.description: Optional per-arrival spawn points, each {x, y, facing}. Edge entries (north/south/east/west) are selected by the side of this level the player arrives on (crossing a neighbor's east edge lands on this level's west entry); stair entries (stairs_up/stairs_down) are selected explicitly by exits via target_entry. A missing entry falls back to the main spawn.

neighbors.description: Whole-edge map links (the 'ocean'): stepping onto a non-wall cell of a linked border crosses to the neighbor scene at its arrival-side entry (player.entry.<side>, Spawn layer), falling back to its main spawn when unset. A point exit on the same cell wins over the edge rule. Because every crossing on one edge lands on the same cell, that entry must be walkable; the compiler refuses to build a link whose used entry is a wall. Empty string or absent = no link on that edge.

exits.description: List of invisible scene-transition triggers (doors, elevators, stairs you paint yourself). The trigger keeps the terrain art painted underneath and never stamps its own tile. A trigger on a linked border cell wins over the neighbors edge rule.

tunnel.description: Two-way tunnel id linking this exit to exactly one return exit in the target scene (same id on both mouths, mutual targets, each landing on the other's gate). Absent = one-way exit.

target_entry.description: Optional named landing: resolve to the destination's player.entry key (or its main spawn when unset) instead of target_x/target_y. Cannot combine with tunnel.

objects.description: Semantic objects and entities placed in the level

properties.description: Engine-mapped actor fields. entity_id/display_name/battle/ai/dialogue/shop/save/quest_var/quest_val are the original slots; actor_id/facing/flags/visual/hp/max_hp/gold_reward/reward_currency are full-fidelity slots so JSON roundtrips the C rows (see tools/level_compiler/decompile.py). overworld_sprite/animation_frames select the SPRITE_KIND_* render.

enemy_type.description: Explicit enemy-type id (screens/enemy_types/<id>.json) for type=enemy placements. Wins over the ENTITY_ID_X naming convention when resolving shared overworld art.

actor_id.description: Stable persistent instance id (defeat tracking). Must be unique across scenes when nonzero.

visual.description: ASCII fallback glyph (semantic buffer + ASCII-kind actors)

regions.description: Semantic zones for LLM contextual awareness and gameplay triggers

entry_spawn.description: A named arrival spawn point {x, y, facing}.
